content: The dataset contains 187,362 loan records spanning from April 2022 to March 2025 across two primary entities.
The 'hfc' entity is the largest by volume, with the home_purchase product alone accounting for 52,618 loans and ₹70.86B in disbursements.
Average yields differ significantly by entity: 15.13% for the 'hfc' housing book compared to 20.60% for the 'finserve' vehicle and MSME book.
The 'hfc' entity maintains a conservative average LTV of 45.08%, while the 'finserve' entity operates at a higher risk profile with 68.01% LTV.
As of March 2025, the 'finserve' entity reported a bounce rate of 34.15%, which is significantly higher than the 25.32% recorded for 'hfc'.
Maharashtra and Rajasthan are the top states by disbursement, contributing ₹20.23B and ₹19.72B respectively to the portfolio.
Asset quality in the housing book ('hfc') is strong, with Stage 3 exposure totaling approximately ₹831.6M against an AUM of ₹85.14B (approx. 0.98% GNPA).
The 'hfc' book has a much longer average tenure of 156.88 months compared to the 'finserve' book's average of 55.54 months.
Always filter by 'entity' (hfc vs finserve) when analyzing yields or risk, as they represent distinct business models (housing vs vehicle/MSME).
Assets Under Management (AUM) must be calculated by summing disbursed_amount only for loans with status 'active' or 'npa'.
Stage 3 (NPA) is defined by DPD buckets npa_90, npa_180, and npa_360_plus, representing loans overdue by more than 90 days.
Housing finance companies typically follow IndAS 109, requiring significantly higher Provision Coverage Ratios (PCR) for Stage 3 assets (approx. 40%).
The 'is_ntc' flag identifies New-to-Credit borrowers (Bureau Score 0), a segment often targeted for micro-housing to drive financial inclusion.
In this portfolio, ~81% of borrowers are self-employed; monitoring 'employment_type' is critical as this segment is more sensitive to economic volatility.
DSA-sourced loans often exhibit higher delinquency rates than direct sales; performance should be monitored via the 'sourcing_channel_performance' table.
Loan-to-Value (LTV) is stored as a decimal (e.g., 0.45 = 45%); the median LTV of ~45% suggests a very high equity buffer from borrowers.
The industry benchmark for collection efficiency in affordable housing is >95%; 'hfc' is aligned with this at 95.31% as of March 2025.
Industry-standard bounce rates for retail lending usually hover around 20%; 'finserve's' 34% rate indicates a higher-than-average presentation risk.
Credit agencies view a single-state concentration of >15% of AUM as a risk; Maharashtra's concentration should be monitored as it nears this threshold.
Yields for used CV and MSME lending in the Indian NBFC sector typically range from 18% to 25% to cover higher operational and credit costs.
For reporting purposes, the Indian Fiscal Year (FY) runs from April to March; FY25 data covers April 2024 through March 2025.
